fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of obstructions at all times could significantly improve emergency vehicle ingress and egress, particularly given the limited options for rear access. Posting clearly visible address markers at the street frontage and at the driveway entrance would support rapid navigation by responding units. Where pedestrian walkways connect the main building to the detached structure, keeping those pathways unobstructed may assist personnel movement during operations. Confirming that the driveway width and surface condition support large emergency vehicle access could further enhance response effectiveness across the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Fuel Continuity; Single Access Route; Defensible Space; Scattered Shrubs; Open Fuel Break
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the density of brush and vegetation in direct contact with or immediately adjacent to the structure would meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce opportunities for fire to transition toward the building. Where shrubs and other vegetation are concentrated near improvements, increasing separation between plant groupings and the structure may reduce fuel continuity and limit the potential for fire spread through connected vegetation. Maintaining the existing open terrain and any natural fuel breaks on the property could support suppression operations and provide firefighters with safer working conditions. Given that the property is served by a single access route, keeping that route clear of encroaching vegetation along its edges would support both firefighter access and evacuation. Continued management of vegetation within the immediate structure perimeter, combined with preserving open areas that interrupt fuel continuity, would support long-term wildfire resilience and improve overall property preparedness.
